title: Pair creation with a recoiling target
promptMarkdown: A photon hits a target of invariant mass M initially at rest and creates a pair of particles of mass m while leaving the target species unchanged:$\gamma+M\to M+m+m$. Neglect binding energy and assume other conservation laws permit the channel. Derive the photon threshold energy. Evaluate it for $M=m$ and find the leading heavy-target limit. Explain why an isolated photon in vacuum cannot create the pair and why a threshold calculation does not give the reaction rate.
hintLadder: Compute the invariant before worrying about laboratory product velocities.
At threshold the massive products share one velocity in the laboratory because they are mutually at rest in the centre-of-momentum frame.
Compare the invariant of one photon with that of a massive pair.
